findings.description: George's former absent-mindedness becomes laziness.

contexts.japanese: かつての僕は、いとこの中で最年長ではあっても、いつもぼんやりしているうだつの上がらない男だったよ。

contexts.japanesePS3: かつての僕は、いとこの中で最年長ではあっても、いつもぼんやりしているうだつの上がらない男だったよ。
contexts.WH: "No, it's okay.  I realize it myself.  Back then, I might have been the oldest of the cousins, but I was still a lazy, hopeless man.
contexts.MG: Back then, I might have been the oldest of the cousins, but I was still a lazy, hopeless person.
contexts.UP: Back then, I might have been the oldest of the cousins, but I was still a lazy, hopeless man.

MG.translation: "No, it's okay. I realize it myself. Back then, I might have been the oldest of the cousins, but I was still a lazy, hopeless person. ...And it wasn't just with the cousins. At home, at school...I was like that everywhere."

UP.japanese: 「いや、いいんだ。自分でもわかってる。かつての僕は、いとこの中で最年長ではあっても、いつもぼんやりしているうだつの上がらない男だったよ。……それは何もいとこの中だけの話じゃない。家でも学校でも、全てでそうだったさ」
UP.translation: "No, it's okay. I realize it myself. Back then, I might have been the oldest of the cousins, but I was still a lazy, hopeless man. ......And it wasn't just with the cousins. At home, at school—I was like that everywhere."

findings.sourceReading: いつもぼんやりしているうだつの上がらない男 portrays someone habitually absent-minded or vague and getting nowhere.
findings.alternative: Lazy, hopeless retains lack of achievement but adds unwillingness to exert himself in place of absent-mindedness.

findings.description: Despite his cowardice becomes because of it and contempt becomes hatred.

contexts.japanese:
そのくせ、自分はこんなにも紳士的なのに、どうして彼女が出来ないのかと一方的に思い込み、
最後には、世間の女性は全て、男を見る目がないなんて勝手に決めつけ、勝手に蔑み始める。
contexts.japanesePC: そのくせ、自分はこんなにも紳士的なのに、どうして彼女が出来ないのかと一方的に思い込み、最後には、世間の女性は全て、男を見る目がないなんて勝手に決めつけ、勝手に蔑み始める。.........これが本当の、情けない男ってもんさ。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
そのくせ、自分はこんなにも紳士的なのに、どうして彼女が出来ないのかと一方的に思い込み、
最後には、世間の女性は全て、男を見る目がないなんて勝手に決めつけ、勝手に蔑み始める。
contexts.WH: Because of that, I started to wonder why I couldn't get a girlfriend if I was so gentlemanly, and I eventually came to the conclusion that all the women in the world had no taste, and started to hate all of them...stupidly.  .........That's what a truly pathetic man looks like."
contexts.MG:
Because of that, I started to wonder why I couldn't get a girlfriend if I was so gentlemanly,
and I eventually came to the conclusion that all the women in the world had no taste, and started to hate all of them, ...selfishly.
contexts.UP:
Because of that, I started to wonder why I couldn't get a lover if I was so gentlemanly,
and I eventually came to the conclusion that all the women in the world had no taste, and started to hate all of them...stupidly.
contexts.note: Full continuous source-first reading completed in durable agent reports. Parent checked canonical outcomes, introduced flags and exact PC/PS3 edition differences. Yellow PC material excluded from defect counts; conservative inherited candidates remain pending.

MG.japanese: 「そんな男を、紳士的な、奥手な男と呼ぶんだろうね。………とんでもない。ただの臆病者さ。そのくせ、自分はこんなにも紳士的なのに、どうして彼女が出来ないのかと一方的に思い込み、最後には、世間の女性は全て、男を見る目がないなんて勝手に決めつけ、勝手に蔑み始める。………これが本当の、情けない男ってもんさ」
MG.translation: "You might call a man like that "gentlemanly" or "a late bloomer". ......Ridiculous. I was just a coward. Because of that, I started to wonder why I couldn't get a girlfriend if I was so gentlemanly, and I eventually came to the conclusion that all the women in the world had no taste, and started to hate all of them, ...selfishly. ......That's what a truly pathetic man looks like."

UP.japanese: 「そんな男を、紳士的な、奥手な男と呼ぶんだろうね。………とんでもない。ただの臆病者さ。そのくせ、自分はこんなにも紳士的なのに、どうして彼女が出来ないのかと一方的に思い込み、最後には、世間の女性は全て、男を見る目がないなんて勝手に決めつけ、勝手に蔑み始める。………これが本当の、情けない男ってもんさ」
UP.translation: "You might call a man like that "gentlemanly" or "a late bloomer". .........Ridiculous. I was just a coward. Because of that, I started to wonder why I couldn't get a lover if I was so gentlemanly, and I eventually came to the conclusion that all the women in the world had no taste, and started to hate all of them...stupidly. .........That's what a truly pathetic man looks like."

findings.sourceReading: そのくせ contrasts his cowardice with his conceited demand for a girlfriend. He then arbitrarily decides women cannot judge men and begins to despise them: 蔑み.
findings.alternative: The psychological sequence can support a causal inference and hatred is close to contempt, but because of that explicitly replaces the concessive link and hate intensifies the reported attitude.

contexts.UP: She might have seemed confused, but she actually did understand what Erika was saying.

MG.japanese: 熊沢は脂汗を浮かべながら、取り繕うように笑う…。彼女は一見、混乱している風を装っているが、実際にはヱリカの話が理解できていた。……実際、彼女は、右代宮金蔵が六軒島に居を移す前からあった悪食島伝説と、金蔵の出所不明の莫大な金塊と、それを授けた黄金の魔女の伝説が、……どのように変遷していったか、おぼろげながら、理解しているのだ。
MG.translation: Kumasawa laughed to smooth it over, wiping away a cold sweat... She might have seemed confused, but she actually did understand what Erika was saying. ...In truth, she had been vaguely aware of how the legend of Akujikishima, which had been around before Ushiromiya Kinzo had come to Rokkenjima, and the legend of the Golden Witch, the story of the woman who had given Kinzo a vast quantity of gold, ...had both transformed.

UP.japanese: 熊沢は脂汗を浮かべながら、取り繕うように笑う…。彼女は一見、混乱している風を装っているが、実際にはヱリカの話が理解できていた。……実際、彼女は、右代宮金蔵が六軒島に居を移す前からあった悪食島伝説と、金蔵の出所不明の莫大な金塊と、それを授けた黄金の魔女の伝説が、……どのように変遷していったか、おぼろげながら、理解しているのだ。
UP.translation: Kumasawa laughed to smooth it over, wiping away a cold sweat... She might have seemed confused, but she actually did understand what Erika was saying. ......In truth, she did have a rough understanding of how the legend of Akujikijima, which had been around before Ushiromiya Kinzo had come to Rokkenjima, and the legend of the Golden Witch, the story of the woman who had given Kinzo a vast quantity of gold, ......had changed over time.

findings.sourceReading: 混乱している風を装っている expressly identifies an appearance of confusion that she is putting on despite understanding.
findings.alternative: Her smoothing-over laughter, sweat and unwillingness to acknowledge the explanation remain. Yet might have seemed confused does not state intentional performance.
